Then, in the backward pass, he goes from right to left. For each student i, if their rating is higher than the next student's, they should get more than candies[i+1] + 1. So the two passes together ensure that each student's candy count is higher than both neighbors. That should satisfy the problem's condition.

Wait, but in the forward pass, he's using >= instead of >. Let me check the code. Oh, he has if arr[i] >= arr[i-1]. So if the current rating is equal to the previous, he still increases the candies. But the problem states that higher ratings should get more than their neighbors. So if two students have the same rating, the one on the right shouldn't get more than the left.
